notes: Good early aggression with repeated Sable R&D runs and naked-remote checks, but turns 10-11 were spent clicking for credits while holding 11-23 credits and a full grip instead of pressuring a Corp with 28+ credits.
Simple score-out plan that worked; installed and advanced a Hybrid Release in a naked remote on turn 1, and ran on a thin economy, but the passive Runner never punished it.

After losing Buzzsaw to Ballista, the Runner clicked for credits for twenty turns up to 89 credits with a full grip, never installing anything or contesting the Corp's remote scores; the only runs were single breakerless facechecks into ETR ice.
Solid fast-advance-style play scoring out of Hagen- and Ansel-protected remotes, with good use of Ansel's no-steal subroutine; economy ran very thin (0 credits at times) but never cost a score.

Consistent R&D/HQ pressure through cheap ice with Tremolo and Docklands Pass won quickly; the Runner sat on several tags with 1-3 credits against a rich Corp and drew into a full grip, which was risky but unpunished.

The Corp never got its economy going (0-5 credits all game), left Project Ingatan sitting un-advanced behind a single barrier after Marjanah landed, and then spent its last turns icing an empty remote while R&D had one Wave and HQ held an agenda.

Strong sustained R&D pressure with Nanuq, Sipa swaps and a Self-modifying Code into Gauss; late it ran broke and piled up Funhouse tags against a recovering Corp, and spent a second HQ run re-accessing the same card.

Early unblocked R&D digging was sensible, but from turn 9 the Runner clicked for credits for nine straight turns up to 48 credits with a full grip and two breakers, never contesting the remote where the Corp scored its last 5 points.

The Corp stayed at 0-4 credits all game, hoarded several agendas in HQ behind one Hafrun instead of trying to score them, and wasted its last turn's money on a Neurospike with no effect, after which the Runner took three agendas from HQ in one turn.

Reasonable Personal Evolution grind with iced remotes and a Saisentan hit, but the Corp ran on 1-7 credits and used Longevity Serum to bin two agendas into an unprotected Archives, giving the Runner 4 free points (the PE damage on the steal then flatlined them).
Clean play: never-exposed install-and-score of two Post-Truth Dividends, then a two-ice remote used to score out; a few idle credit clicks while already at 11-15 credits.

Good start reaching 4 points off R&D, but after trading Buzzsaw for SDS Drone Deployment the Runner spent ~15 turns paying Banner 2 credits per HQ run (often twice a turn, re-seeing the same cards) while broke and drawing into discards, then ran into a known Hammer a second time; it never built a rig to contest the remote.

The Corp spent most of its clicks and credits trashing tagged-Runner resources, leaving itself at 0-3 credits for the rest of the game, and twice put agendas in a remote with only cheap taxing ice; the final Next Big Thing went in at 1 credit with no way to rez the outer ice, giving the Runner at 6 points the win.

After a reasonable start, the Runner ran into a known Anemone on Server 4 about a dozen times only to take net damage and jack out, binning its own breakers and economy, and on turn 17 ignored a naked remote holding a twice-advanced Fujii Asset Retrieval that the Corp scored for the win next turn.

Built a sensible rig (Revolver, Shibboleth, Docklands Pass) and won with a big HQ double steal and an R&D hit; it facechecked an unrezzed Jinteki remote ice with no killer and lost four cards to Karuna, and ignored a naked advanced card for a turn spent drawing.

Rich, efficient Haas-Bioroid play that scored out of a Vertigo-protected remote and used Drafter installs well; minor oddities include clicking for credits at 14-18 credits and over-drawing into end-of-turn discards.

Kept a slow single-access R&D/Archives lock on a Corp stuck at 1 credit and eventually won, but it let the Corp score 5 points early from an Akhet remote, paid 2 credits nearly every turn to clear harmless tags, sat on a full grip and drew into discards for a dozen turns instead of building up for multi-access.

The Corp stayed at 0-5 credits, twice fired Neurospike with no agenda scored, put three ice on an empty Server 3, and never tried to score; the agendas it drew sat in HQ behind one Ivik until the Runner took them for the win.
Won by scoring out of Ansel/Vertigo remotes and using Ansel installs well, but a 0-3 credit midgame left Ansel on HQ unrezzed while two Architect Deployment Tests sat in HQ and were stolen.

The Runner took five Funhouse tags early on repeated R&D runs while broke, then spent about ten turns at 0-2 credits clicking for credits to clear tags without ever playing its three-card grip; it won only by repeatedly running the Corp's tag-ice remote and a naked remote.
